subject: vintage

samsara-2020.name: SAMsARA Wine, The 2020 Vintage Growing Season: A Santa Barbara County Retrospective
samsara-2020.note: Winery blog. Covers Santa Barbara County, mostly Santa Maria Valley and Sta. Rita Hills fruit.

wia-2020.name: Wine Industry Advisor, Santa Barbara Vintners Impressed by Quality of 2020 Vintage (Santa Barbara County Vintners Association)

vinous-2020.name: Vinous, Santa Barbara: A Rare Bright Spot for California in 2020 (Aug 2022)

independent-2020.name: Santa Barbara Independent, Rescuing California's Hellish 2020 Wine Vintage (18 Nov 2020)

claims.claim: The season started typically for Santa Barbara County, with moderate weather and normal bud break. Santa Barbara ran much cooler than most of California until heat arrived in mid-August.
claims.note: Two sources, but neither gives winter rain, frost or flowering.

claims.claim: Heat spikes from mid-August, including a Labor Day heat wave, sped up ripening. Fruit came in about two weeks ahead of plan, and many growers picked earlier than they intended.
Wildfires that hit Northern California spared Santa Barbara County. Smoke darkened skies at high elevations, but growers and critics saw no smoke taint in the grapes or wines.
claims.note: Independent notes smoke taint was absent 'with rare exceptions'. Vinous says smoke taint is not fully understood, and some winemakers destemmed Pinot as a precaution.

claims.claim: Yields were slightly below average, but not by much.
claims.note: Winery and trade-group statements. No tonnage figures found.

claims.claim: Chardonnay was the standout. Thicker skins coped with the late heat, and the wines are consistent. Sta. Rita Hills Chardonnays are singled out as very fine.
claims.note: One critic. Vinous paraphrase from a page read in full.

claims.claim: Pinot Noir is more variable. The best wines are deep and rich. Thin skins made the heat harder on Pinot, and some wines show heat stress.
claims.note: One critic. Samsara calls its Santa Maria Valley Rancho La Vina Pinot one of its finest, so producers are more upbeat.

claims.claim: Santa Barbara County Vintners Association members called quality high across the region. Some winemakers said 2020 could set the standard for cooler-climate wines from the county.
claims.note: Trade group and producer opinion, made weeks after harvest.

conflicts: Pinot Noir: Vinous finds it variable with heat stress in places. Producers (SAMsARA, SBCVA) are more positive.
gaps: No winter or spring rainfall, frost or flowering detail found for 2020.
No harvest dates beyond 'about two weeks early'.
No tonnage or yield figures. The county crop report was not read.
Nothing split between Santa Maria Valley and Sta. Rita Hills. Sources speak for the county.
Vinous page was read through a fetch summary, not line by line.
Filed under central-coast but the sources cover Santa Barbara County only.

sheet.vintage: Santa Barbara stayed cool until mid-August, then heat pulled harvest early. Smoke from the 2020 fires did not reach the vines. Chardonnay was the standout.
